clauses.text: (a) A standard hook may have a 180° bend plus an extension of at least 4 bar diameters, but not less than 65 mm, at the free end of the bar.
clauses.notes:
Hook - A curved or bent portion at the end of a rebar.

Standard hook - A reinforcing bar's end that is bent in a specified shape and length according to code requirements.

Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend

clauses.text: (b) A standard hook may have a 90° bend plus an extension of at least 12 bar diameters at the free end of the bar.
clauses.notes:
Hook - A curved or bent portion at the end of a rebar.

Standard hook - A reinforcing bar's end that is bent in a specified shape and length according to code requirements.

Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend

clauses.text: Standard hooks in case of stirrup and tie anchorage: (c)(i) if the diameter of stirrup or tie bar is 16 mm or smaller, the hooks shall have a 90° bend plus an extension of at least 6 bar diameters at the free end of the bar
clauses.notes:
Stirrups and ties - small reinforcing bars used to confine and support the main steel bars in beams and columns.
Anchorage - how the ends of stirrups and ties are bent, hooked, or extended.

Bend angle - the angle through which a reinforcing bar, stirrup, tie, or hook is bent from its original straight direction.

Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend point at the free end of the bar

clauses.text: Standard hooks in case of stirrup and tie anchorage: (c)(ii) if the diameter of stirrup or tie bar is between 19 mm to 25 mm, the hooks shall have a 90° bend plus an extension of at least 12 bar diameters at the free end of the bar
clauses.notes:
Stirrups and ties - small reinforcing bars used to confine and support the main steel bars in beams and columns.
Anchorage - how the ends of stirrups and ties are bent, hooked, or extended.
Bend angle - the angle through which a reinforcing bar, stirrup, tie, or hook is bent from its original straight direction.
Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend point at the free end of the bar

clauses.text: Standard hooks in case of stirrup and tie anchorage: (c)(iii) if the diameter of stirrup or tie bar is 25 mm or larger, the hooks shall have a 135° bend plus an extension of at least 6 bar diameters at the free end of the bar
clauses.notes:
Stirrups and ties - small reinforcing bars used to confine and support the main steel bars in beams and columns.
Anchorage - how the ends of stirrups and ties are bent, hooked, or extended.
Bend angle - the angle through which a reinforcing bar, stirrup, tie, or hook is bent from its original straight direction.
Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend point at the free end of the bar

clauses.text: Standard hooks in case of stirrup and tie anchorage: (c)(iv) For closed ties and continuously wound ties, the hooks shall have a 135° bend plus an extension of at least 6 bar diameters, but not less than 75 mm.
clauses.notes:
Stirrups and ties - small reinforcing bars used to confine and support the main steel bars in beams and columns.
Anchorage - how the ends of stirrups and ties are bent, hooked, or extended.
Bend angle - the angle through which a reinforcing bar, stirrup, tie, or hook is bent from its original straight direction.
Extension length - length of the bar beyond the bend point at the free end of the bar
Closed ties - Ties that form a completely closed loop around the main reinforcement bars in a column. Their ends are anchored with proper hooks so the tie fully encloses the bars.
Continuously wound ties - Spiral-type reinforcement made from a continuous bar or wire wrapped repeatedly around the longitudinal reinforcement in a helical or spiral form. Instead of separate individual ties, the reinforcement is continuous along the height or length of the member.

clauses.text: (d) Seismic hook is defined as a hook on a stirrup, hoop, or crosstie having a bend not less than 135°, except that circular hoops shall have a bend not less than 90°. Hooks shall have a six-diameter (but not less than 75 mm ) extension that engages the longitudinal reinforcement and projects into the interior of the stirrup or hoop.
clauses.notes:
Seismic hook - a special hook used on stirrups, hoops, or crossties designed to perform under seismic (earthquake) loading conditions
Stirrup - a transverse reinforcing bar used to resist shear forces in a beam or column
Hoop - a closed loop of reinforcing bar enclosing longitudinal bars
Crosstie - a bar with hooks at each end used to tie opposite sides of a reinforcement cage together
